# A global critical cover does not transfer closed point incidence to rate capture

This is an exact counterexample to one proposed AUXILIARY implication:
ordinary closed-halfspace depth of a limiting rate component, together
with a genuine global critical cap cover, does not control actual moving
cap selections at that component. It uses a unique GLOBAL deepest point,
a finite balanced menu, and equal actual critical cap masses. It is not
in the OC-bad numerical regime and does not assert joint parameter/body
stationarity. The missing cap blow-up information is exhibited exactly.

## 1. The actual core and its unique global deepest point

Use the unpadded centrally symmetric core from
candidate eb56baa1ba0b7480:

    K_0=A_lambda={(x,y):0<=x<=1, |y|<=x+lambda},
    K_1=B_lambda=c+(A_lambda-A_lambda)/2,
    K_2=D_lambda=2c-A_lambda,
    c=(1,0),       0<lambda<=1/4.

These are exactly the sampled fibers of an actual convex body at bases
0,1,2. Their total volume is M=7/2+6lambda. The point
Y=(z=1,x=1,y=0) has depth Q=M/2 by central symmetry.

It is the unique deepest point. Each endpoint fiber can be isolated
by a pure-base cap and has mass 1+2lambda<Q. At base1, if X!=c, choose
a through-Y halfspace with continuous normal in direction X-c. It
has mass Q. Moving its threshold a positive distance toward X excludes
a positive own-fiber slab, because c is interior to B_lambda. The
halfspace through (1,X) therefore has mass less than Q. This proves
uniqueness without restricting ambient halfspace orientations.

## 2. A finite actual critical menu with balanced continuous normals

Fix a=4/5 and define two caps

    G_+={y+a lambda(z-1)>=0},
    G_-={-y+a lambda(z-1)>=0}.                           (1)

Both pass through Y, so both have ACTUAL volume Q. Their continuous
normals are e_y and -e_y. Their proper total coareas are identical,
by reflection y->-y, and their own traces pass through the interior
point c of B_lambda.

Add the two caps

    J_+={x+(1/2-1)z>=1/2},
    J_-={-x-(1/2-1)z>=-1/2}.                           (2)

They are opposite through-Y caps, each of mass Q, with continuous
normals e_x and -e_x and equal coareas within this pair.

Give G_+,G_- cap-law weights 19/40 each, and J_+,J_- weights 1/40 each.
These can be obtained by the actual harmonic coarea normalization:
if S_H denotes each total coarea, take rho_H proportional to theta_H S_H.
Within each opposite-continuous-normal pair the coareas and theta weights
are equal, so sum rho_H u_H=0 exactly. The four continuous normals span
R^2 and all rho weights are positive.

This is a genuine finite global critical cover. At the only deepest
base, any X!=c has positive margin in at least one of the four spanning
normal directions; the corresponding translated through-(1,X) cap has
mass below Q. The two other bases have strict pure-base gaps. No padded
local anchor is used.

## 3. A real rate component and its actual cap selections

Take a normalized positive affine denominator

    L_lambda=C_lambda(x+epsilon_lambda),
    min L_lambda=exp(-T/lambda),                         (3)

with any fixed T>0. The geometric normalization and inverse/log bounds
are proved in the preceding examples. Only A_lambda has a zero-set
defect: the other two fibers have x>=1/2. Its surface defect is
2T delta_(z=0,x=0,y=0,rate=T), and its canonical inverse density is

    v_e(R)=2 delta_w*,      0<R<T,
    e=e_x, w*=(0,0,0).                                 (4)

At a fixed rate R, the actual slice has
x=C_lambda^(-1)exp(-R/lambda)-epsilon_lambda and
-(x+lambda)<=y<=x+lambda. On the base z=0, (1) becomes

    G_+: y>=a lambda,
    G_-: y<=-a lambda.

As lambda->0 at fixed positive R, each cap retains fraction
(1-a)/2=1/10 of this slice. Thus the ACTUAL selected inverse densities
are

    v_(e,G_+)(R)=v_(e,G_-)(R)=(1/10)v_e(R).             (5)

Their cap normals are nonparallel to e; the logarithmic section defects
are zero, in agreement with the capwise kernel. The fractional selection
is retained in the actual exterior facet selector and in its uniform
inverse kernel. It is not a supporting allocation convention.

At the same zero point, J_+ strictly misses and J_- strictly captures.
Therefore

    v_(e,J_+)(R)=0,
    v_(e,J_-)(R)=v_e(R).

Every nonzero captured part is noninside relative to e. The total law
therefore satisfies

    v_e^noninside(R)=v_good(R)=(3/25)v_e(R).             (6)

Indeed (19/20)(1/10)+1/40=3/25.

## 4. The failed closed-incidence lower bound

The limiting halfspaces of G_+,G_- are respectively {y>=0} and {y<=0}.
Both contain w* on their boundary. J_- contains it strictly and J_+
misses it strictly. Hence

    theta{H noninside relative to e, w* in CLOSED H}=39/40. (7)

The limiting rate component is a single atom, with ordinary closed
halfspace depth one at w*. Even using only the weaker dimensional-lift
constant Gamma_(d-1)=Gamma_1=1/2 would predict the proposed lower bound

    v_e^noninside(R)
       >=(1/2)(39/40)v_e(R)=(39/80)v_e(R).

Equation (6) disproves it, since 3/25<39/80. The same failure holds with
the improved v_good. The problem is not an inside exception: both
problematic caps have nonparallel continuous normals. Their limiting
closed incidence does not remember their distinct positions in the
collapsing y-coordinate.

At the level of an actual affine blow-up y/lambda, their limits are
Y>=a and Y<=-a in the interval [-1,1]. They both MISS its centroid.
There is therefore no contradiction with ordinary Grünbaum. It is the
unjustified use of the projected atom's closed incidence that fails.

## 5. Scope of this global-cover test

The example has beta=1/2, not beta<Gamma_2/2. It is not a joint selected
minimum for the nonconstant denominator (3). In fact the original mixed
centroid is Y, so L=1 is a fixed-body global logarithmic-parameter
minimum by Jensen; the displayed affine denominator has no claimed
same-separator parameter stationarity. No actual contact-row transport
for (3) is manufactured.

The certificate proves the stated narrower point: GLOBAL deepestness,
a finite spanning balanced critical cover, equal individual cap masses,
proper source traces, the exact rate kernel, and a convex lift of the
projected rate law do not justify the closed-incidence transfer in
Section 4. A proposed selected-minimum proof may still use additional
canonical parameter/source equations, but it must do so explicitly, or
retain an ACTUAL common blow-up of the slice bodies and cap hyperplanes.
